grammar.title: Giving Directions with the Imperative
grammar.explanation: In Italian, the imperative mood is used to give directions. For 'tu' (informal): gira (turn), vai (go), attraversa (cross). For 'Lei' (formal/polite): giri, vada, attraversi. Common direction phrases: 'gira a destra/sinistra' (turn right/left), 'vai dritto' (go straight), 'attraversa la strada' (cross the street). The formal imperative is often used when giving directions to strangers.
